patterns.name: Bearish Belt Hold
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Opened at the high, closed at the low.
patterns.ruleText: Price opens at or near the session high with almost no upper wick, then sells off hard to close near the low with almost no lower wick, a full bearish body. Confirmation is the next candle closing below this candle's low.

patterns.name: Bullish Belt Hold
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Opened at the low, closed at the high.
patterns.ruleText: Price opens at or near the session low with almost no lower wick, then rallies hard to close near the high with almost no upper wick, a full bullish body. Confirmation is the next candle closing above this candle's high.

patterns.name: Dragonfly Doji
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Drove to support, buyers took it all back.
patterns.ruleText: The open and close land at the top of the range with almost no upper wick, while a long lower wick shows sellers pushed price down to support before buyers reclaimed it entirely. Confirmation is the next candle closing higher.

patterns.name: Gravestone Doji
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Buyers pushed into resistance, sellers erased the gain.
patterns.ruleText: The open and close land at the bottom of the range with almost no lower wick, while a long upper wick shows buyers pushed price into resistance before sellers took it all back. Confirmation is the next candle closing lower.

patterns.name: Long-Legged Doji
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Wild swings both ways, sellers won the next bar.
patterns.ruleText: The open and close land near the middle of an unusually wide range, with long wicks on both sides showing violent back-and-forth trading and no net winner. Confirmation is the next candle closing below this candle's low.

patterns.name: Doji
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Open and close matched, then sellers took control.
patterns.ruleText: A doji forms when the open and close are virtually equal, showing buyers and sellers reached a standstill. At resistance after an uptrend, that hesitation matters; confirmation is the next candle closing below the doji's low.

patterns.name: Hammer
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Sellers pushed it down, buyers slammed it back up.
patterns.ruleText: After a downtrend, price sells off intraday to test support, then closes back near the candle's high, leaving a lower wick at least twice the real body. Confirmation is the next candle closing above the hammer's high.

patterns.name: Hanging Man
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Sharp intraday selloff near the highs, a warning.
patterns.ruleText: Near a resistance zone after an uptrend, price sells off sharply intraday then recovers to close near the open, leaving a lower wick at least twice the small body. Confirmation is the next candle closing below this candle's low.

patterns.name: High Wave
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Extreme swings both ways, buyers won the next bar.
patterns.ruleText: A small real body sits inside exceptionally long wicks on both sides, showing extreme back-and-forth trading beyond a normal spinning top. Near support after a downtrend, confirmation is the next candle closing above this candle's high.

patterns.name: Bearish Marubozu
patterns.context: consolidation above support, tested twice, then a breakdown
patterns.answerLine: Open at the high, close at the low, breakdown.
patterns.ruleText: A full-bodied candle opens at its high and closes at its low with no wicks on either side, showing sellers controlled the entire session. Breaking below support this way is a strong signal; confirmation is the next candle holding below the breakdown.

patterns.name: Bullish Marubozu
patterns.context: consolidation under resistance, tested twice, then a breakout
patterns.answerLine: Open at the low, close at the high, breakout.
patterns.ruleText: A full-bodied candle opens at its low and closes at its high with no wicks on either side, showing buyers controlled the entire session. Breaking above resistance this way is a strong signal; confirmation is the next candle holding above the breakout.

patterns.name: Shooting Star
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Spiked into resistance, gave it all back.
patterns.ruleText: After an uptrend, price spikes into resistance then closes back near the open, leaving an upper wick at least twice the small body and almost no lower shadow. Confirmation is the next candle closing below this candle's low.

patterns.name: Spinning Top
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before
patterns.answerLine: Small body, big wicks both ways, momentum stalled.
patterns.ruleText: A small body sits between two wicks of similar, noticeably larger size on both ends, showing neither buyers nor sellers controlled the session. Near resistance after an uptrend, that stall matters; confirmation is the next candle closing lower.

patterns.name: Bearish Engulfing
patterns.context: at resistance after a multi-leg uptrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Second body swallows the first. Sellers took control.
patterns.ruleText: A bullish candle at resistance is followed by a larger bearish candle that opens above the prior close and closes below the prior open, fully engulfing the previous body. Confirmation is the full engulf on a closing basis, not just a wick.

patterns.name: Bearish Harami
patterns.context: at resistance after an uptrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Small body tucked inside the big green candle.
patterns.ruleText: After a long bullish candle at resistance, a small-bodied candle forms whose entire body sits inside the prior candle's body, showing momentum stalling. Confirmation is a bearish close on the following candle that breaks below the small candle's low.

patterns.name: Bullish Engulfing
patterns.context: at support after a multi-leg downtrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Second body swallows the first. Buyers took control.
patterns.ruleText: A bearish candle at support is followed by a larger bullish candle that opens below the prior close and closes above the prior open, fully engulfing the previous body. Confirmation is the full engulf on a closing basis, not just a wick.

patterns.name: Bullish Harami
patterns.context: at support after a downtrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Small body tucked inside the big red candle.
patterns.ruleText: After a long bearish candle at support, a small-bodied candle forms whose entire body sits inside the prior candle's body, showing momentum stalling. Confirmation is a bullish close on the following candle that breaks above the small candle's high.

patterns.name: Dark Cloud Cover
patterns.context: at resistance after an uptrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Gapped up, then closed deep into the green body.
patterns.ruleText: A bullish candle at resistance is followed by a bearish candle that opens above the prior close and closes below the midpoint of the prior candle's body, without fully engulfing it. Confirmation is a close below that midpoint.

patterns.name: Harami Cross
patterns.context: at support after a downtrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: A doji sits dead center of the first body.
patterns.ruleText: A bearish harami where the second candle is a doji, its open and close essentially equal, sitting fully inside the prior candle's large body. The doji shows indecision after a strong move; confirmation is a bullish close beyond the doji's high.

patterns.name: In-Neck Line
patterns.context: within an established downtrend, at a fresh swing low
patterns.answerLine: Gap down, close barely pokes above yesterday's close.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, a long bearish candle is followed by a small bullish candle that gaps down at the open and closes only marginally above the prior candle's close, barely penetrating its body. Confirmation is the next candle breaking below the prior low.

patterns.name: Matching Low
patterns.context: at the bottom of a downtrend, two candles closing at the same price
patterns.answerLine: Two candles close at the identical price. Floor confirmed.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, two candles close at essentially the same low price, marking a level where selling repeatedly stops. Confirmation is the next candle closing above both matching closes.

patterns.name: On-Neck Line
patterns.context: within an established downtrend, at a fresh swing low
patterns.answerLine: Gap down sold; close lands on the prior low.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, a long bearish candle is followed by a small bullish candle that gaps down at the open and closes at or just above the prior candle's low, forming a flat neckline. Confirmation is the next candle breaking below that low.

patterns.name: Piercing Line
patterns.context: at support after a downtrend, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Gapped down, then closed deep into the red body.
patterns.ruleText: A bearish candle at support is followed by a bullish candle that opens below the prior close and closes above the midpoint of the prior candle's body, without fully engulfing it. Confirmation is a close above that midpoint.

patterns.name: Separating Lines
patterns.context: within an established uptrend, after a one-bar pullback
patterns.answerLine: Same opening price, opposite colors, trend resumes hard.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend, a bearish pullback candle is followed by a bullish candle that opens at essentially the same price as the pullback candle's open, then rallies to a strong higher close. Confirmation is the second candle's close well above its own open.

patterns.name: Thrusting Line
patterns.context: within an established downtrend, at a fresh swing low
patterns.answerLine: Gap down, close stays under the midpoint.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, a long bearish candle is followed by a bullish candle that gaps down at the open and closes above the prior close but still below the midpoint of the prior candle's body. Confirmation is the next candle breaking below the prior low.

patterns.name: Tweezer Bottom
patterns.context: at support after a downtrend, matching lows printed twice
patterns.answerLine: Two candles, same low, buyers defended the floor twice.
patterns.ruleText: Two consecutive candles print essentially the same low at support, one bearish and one bullish, showing sellers failed twice to push lower. Confirmation is the second candle closing higher than it opened, above the first candle's close.

patterns.name: Tweezer Top
patterns.context: at resistance after an uptrend, matching highs printed twice
patterns.answerLine: Two candles, same high, sellers defended the ceiling twice.
patterns.ruleText: Two consecutive candles print essentially the same high at resistance, one bullish and one bearish, showing buyers failed twice to push higher. Confirmation is the second candle closing lower than it opened, below the first candle's close.

patterns.name: Evening Doji Star
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice, middle candle is a true doji
patterns.answerLine: True doji gap up, then sellers erase the spike.
patterns.ruleText: A long bullish candle is followed by a true doji (open equals close) that gaps above it, then a bearish candle closing back below the midpoint of the first candle's body. The exact doji marks total indecision before sellers take over.

patterns.name: Evening Star
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice before the pattern forms
patterns.answerLine: Third candle erases the rally into day one's range.
patterns.ruleText: A long bullish candle is followed by a small-bodied candle that gaps above it, then a bearish candle that closes back below the midpoint of the first candle's body. That deep close is the confirmation, not the gap itself.

patterns.name: Morning Doji Star
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice, middle candle is a true doji
patterns.answerLine: True doji gap, then buyers erase the drop.
patterns.ruleText: A long bearish candle is followed by a true doji (open equals close) that gaps below it, then a bullish candle closing back above the midpoint of the first candle's body. The exact doji marks total indecision before buyers take over.

patterns.name: Morning Star
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice before the pattern forms
patterns.answerLine: Third candle closes deep into the first candle's body.
patterns.ruleText: A long bearish candle is followed by a small-bodied candle that gaps below it, then a bullish candle that closes back above the midpoint of the first candle's body. That deep close is the confirmation, not the gap itself.

patterns.name: Three Inside Down
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Third candle closes below the first candle's open.
patterns.ruleText: A long bullish candle is followed by a small bearish candle whose body sits fully inside the first candle's body (a harami), then a third candle closes below the first candle's open. That final close below the open confirms the reversal is holding.

patterns.name: Three Inside Up
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Third candle closes above the first candle's open.
patterns.ruleText: A long bearish candle is followed by a small bullish candle whose body sits fully inside the first candle's body (a harami), then a third candle closes above the first candle's open. That final close above the open confirms the reversal is holding.

patterns.name: Three Outside Down
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Engulfing candle, then a lower close confirms it.
patterns.ruleText: A small bullish candle is engulfed by a larger bearish candle that opens above its close and closes below its open, then a third candle pushes to a lower close. That lower third close confirms sellers are in control, not just one reversal bar.

patterns.name: Three Outside Up
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Engulfing candle, then a higher close confirms it.
patterns.ruleText: A small bearish candle is engulfed by a larger bullish candle that opens below its close and closes above its open, then a third candle pushes to a higher close. That higher third close confirms buyers are in control, not just one reversal bar.

patterns.name: Abandoned Baby (Bearish)
patterns.context: uptrend into resistance, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Doji gaps above, then price gaps back below.
patterns.ruleText: A long bullish candle is followed by a doji that gaps completely above it with no overlap, then a bearish candle that gaps back down below the doji's low. Two clean gaps isolating the doji is what separates this from an ordinary star pattern.

patterns.name: Abandoned Baby (Bullish)
patterns.context: downtrend into support, tested twice
patterns.answerLine: Doji gaps below, then price gaps back above.
patterns.ruleText: A long bearish candle is followed by a doji that gaps completely below it with no overlap, then a bullish candle that gaps back up above the doji's high. Two clean gaps isolating the doji is what separates this from an ordinary star pattern.

patterns.name: Falling Three Methods
patterns.context: established downtrend, brief bounce that holds inside the prior candle's range
patterns.answerLine: Pullback holds inside the range, then a new low.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, one long bearish candle is followed by three small candles that drift higher but stay inside that candle's high-low range, then a fifth long bearish candle closes below the first candle's close. Holding inside the range during the bounce is what confirms the trend never broke.

patterns.name: Rising Three Methods
patterns.context: established uptrend, brief pullback that holds inside the prior candle's range
patterns.answerLine: Pullback holds inside the range, then a new high.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend, one long bullish candle is followed by three small candles that drift lower but stay inside that candle's high-low range, then a fifth long bullish candle closes above the first candle's close. Holding inside the range during the pullback is what confirms the trend never broke.

patterns.name: Upside Tasuki Gap
patterns.context: established uptrend, no prior test of this level
patterns.answerLine: Pullback dips into the gap but doesn't fill it.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend, a bullish candle is followed by another bullish candle that gaps above it, then a bearish candle that pushes back into the gap but closes without fully filling it. The unfilled gap is the confirmation that the uptrend still has control.

patterns.name: Double Bottom
patterns.context: after a steady downtrend, price tests the same support twice, held both times, with a resistance peak between the two troughs
patterns.answerLine: Second bottom held the same price. Resistance peak gave way.
patterns.ruleText: Price falls to support, bounces, then falls again to the same support and holds a second time. Confirmation is a close above the resistance peak formed between the two troughs, not just the second hold itself.

patterns.name: Double Top
patterns.context: after a steady uptrend, price tests the same resistance twice, rejected both times, with a support trough between the two peaks
patterns.answerLine: Second top rejected at the same price. Support trough gave way.
patterns.ruleText: Price rallies to resistance, pulls back, then rallies again to the same resistance and fails a second time. Confirmation is a close below the support trough formed between the two peaks, not just the second rejection itself.

patterns.name: Head and Shoulders
patterns.context: at the top of a sustained uptrend, three peaks form: a left shoulder, a higher head, and a right shoulder back near the shoulder height, separated by two pullbacks that bottom at nearly the same price
patterns.answerLine: Neckline broke. Both shoulders failed to reclaim the head.
patterns.ruleText: Two pullbacks between the shoulders and head form a neckline near the same price. The right shoulder fails to reach the head's high. Confirmation is a close below the neckline, which had held twice before.

patterns.name: Inverse Head and Shoulders
patterns.context: at the bottom of a sustained downtrend, three troughs form: a left shoulder, a lower head, and a right shoulder back near the shoulder depth, separated by two bounces that top out at nearly the same price
patterns.answerLine: Neckline broke up. Right shoulder held well above the head.
patterns.ruleText: Two bounces between the shoulders and head form a neckline near the same price. The right shoulder fails to reach the head's low. Confirmation is a close above the neckline, which had capped price twice before.

patterns.name: Rounding Bottom (Saucer)
patterns.context: after a falling trend, losses shrink bar by bar into a flat plateau, then gains slowly build, tracing a saucer shape over many bars before reaching the neckline resistance
patterns.answerLine: The saucer finished curling up. Momentum flipped up for good.
patterns.ruleText: Instead of a sharp turn, losses shrink into a flat plateau and gains slowly build afterward, tracing a saucer shape over many bars. Confirmation is a close above the neckline resistance that formed over the plateau.

patterns.name: Rounding Top
patterns.context: after a rising trend, gains shrink bar by bar into a flat plateau, then losses slowly build, tracing a dome shape over many bars before reaching the neckline support
patterns.answerLine: The dome finished rolling over. Momentum flipped down for good.
patterns.ruleText: Instead of a sharp turn, gains shrink into a flat plateau and losses slowly build afterward, tracing a dome shape over many bars. Confirmation is a close below the neckline support that formed under the plateau.

patterns.name: Triple Bottom
patterns.context: after a downtrend, price tests the same support three separate times and holds each time, with two bounces topping out at a shared resistance level
patterns.answerLine: Three failed pushes at support. Shared resistance finally broke.
patterns.ruleText: Price falls into the same support three times without breaking through. Confirmation is a close above the resistance level shared by the bounces between those three troughs, showing sellers are exhausted, not just a third hold.

patterns.name: Triple Top
patterns.context: after an uptrend, price tests the same resistance three separate times and is rejected each time, with two pullbacks holding a shared support level
patterns.answerLine: Three failed pushes at resistance. Shared support finally broke.
patterns.ruleText: Price rallies into the same resistance three times without pushing through. Confirmation is a close below the support level shared by the pullbacks between those three peaks, showing buyers are exhausted, not just a third rejection.

patterns.name: Broadening Top (Megaphone)
patterns.context: after an uptrend, three peaks climb progressively higher while the troughs between them fall progressively lower, widening like a megaphone, then a bounce fails to make a new high
patterns.answerLine: Bounce failed to beat the last peak. Widest support broke.
patterns.ruleText: Each swing high gets higher and each swing low gets lower, widening the range. Confirmation comes when a bounce fails to exceed the prior peak and price then closes below the lowest trough of the formation.

patterns.name: Bump and Run Reversal
patterns.context: a steady lead-in uptrend defines a moderate trendline, then price breaks sharply above that trendline's slope into a steep speculative 'bump' rally, before rolling over
patterns.answerLine: Steep bump rolled over. Price broke the lead-in trendline.
patterns.ruleText: A modest uptrend sets a lead-in trendline slope, then price accelerates well above that slope into a steep speculative bump. Confirmation is a close back below the extended lead-in trendline, the 'run' phase, not merely the rollover from the bump's peak.

patterns.name: Diamond Top
patterns.context: after an uptrend, swings widen into a broadening top (each peak higher, each trough lower) then narrow symmetrically into a converging apex, tracing a diamond shape
patterns.answerLine: Diamond apex closed. Price broke below the lower boundary.
patterns.ruleText: Price swings widen (higher highs, lower lows) then contract symmetrically toward a point, forming a diamond outline. Confirmation is a close below the diamond's lower support boundary as the swings converge, not just the narrowing itself.

patterns.name: Bear Flag
patterns.context: sharp downtrend (the flagpole) followed by a tight, upward-drifting consolidation channel
patterns.answerLine: Breakdown clears the flag. Downtrend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: A bear flag is a sharp decline (the pole) followed by a tight, upward-drifting consolidation (the flag) against the trend. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes below the flag's lower boundary, resuming the prior downtrend.

patterns.name: Bearish Pennant
patterns.context: sharp downtrend (the pole) followed by a small symmetrical, converging consolidation
patterns.answerLine: Pennant breaks down. Pole's trend continues.
patterns.ruleText: A bearish pennant is a sharp decline (the pole) followed by a small, symmetrical consolidation whose highs and lows converge toward a point. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes below the pennant's lower boundary and the pole's low.

patterns.name: Bull Flag
patterns.context: sharp uptrend (the flagpole) followed by a tight, downward-drifting consolidation channel
patterns.answerLine: Breakout clears the flag. Uptrend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: A bull flag is a sharp rally (the pole) followed by a tight, downward-drifting consolidation (the flag) against the trend. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes above the flag's upper boundary, resuming the prior uptrend.

patterns.name: Bullish Pennant
patterns.context: sharp uptrend (the pole) followed by a small symmetrical, converging consolidation
patterns.answerLine: Pennant breaks up. Pole's trend continues.
patterns.ruleText: A bullish pennant is a sharp rally (the pole) followed by a small, symmetrical consolidation whose highs and lows converge toward a point. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes above the pennant's upper boundary and the pole's high.

patterns.name: Rectangle (Range Continuation)
patterns.context: uptrend into a horizontal range bounded by clear support and resistance, tested three times each
patterns.answerLine: Range top finally gives way. Trend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: A rectangle is a horizontal range with well-defined, repeatedly tested support and resistance. Continuation of the prior uptrend is confirmed when a candle closes above the range's resistance on an expanding range, rather than the range simply repeating another leg.

patterns.name: Ascending Triangle
patterns.context: uptrend into a flat resistance tested three times while pullback lows keep rising
patterns.answerLine: Flat top, rising floor. Buyers finally break it.
patterns.ruleText: An ascending triangle is a flat resistance level tested repeatedly while each pullback forms a higher low, showing buyers stepping in earlier each time. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes above the flat resistance on an expanding range.

patterns.name: Cup and Handle
patterns.context: uptrend rounding into a U-shaped cup back to the prior high, then a shallow handle just under the rim
patterns.answerLine: Handle holds the rim. Breakout resumes the climb.
patterns.ruleText: A cup and handle is a rounded, U-shaped decline and recovery back toward the prior high (the cup), followed by a shallow pullback near the rim (the handle) that does not revisit the cup's midpoint. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes above the rim.

patterns.name: Descending Triangle
patterns.context: downtrend into a flat support tested three times while rally highs keep falling
patterns.answerLine: Flat floor, falling ceiling. Sellers finally break it.
patterns.ruleText: A descending triangle is a flat support level tested repeatedly while each rally forms a lower high, showing sellers stepping in earlier each time. Continuation is confirmed when a candle closes below the flat support on an expanding range.

patterns.name: Falling Wedge (continuation)
patterns.context: uptrend interrupted by a corrective pullback whose support and resistance lines both fall but converge
patterns.answerLine: Wedge resistance breaks. Uptrend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: A falling wedge inside an uptrend is a corrective pullback where both boundary lines slope downward but the range narrows, resistance falling faster than support. Continuation of the uptrend is confirmed when a candle closes above the wedge's falling resistance line.

patterns.name: Inverse Cup and Handle
patterns.context: downtrend rounding into an upside-down, dome-shaped rally back to the prior low, then a shallow handle just above the rim
patterns.answerLine: Handle fails to reclaim the rim. Downtrend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: An inverse cup and handle is a rounded, dome-shaped rally and decline toward the prior low (the cup), followed by a shallow bounce near the rim (the handle) that does not revisit the dome's midpoint. Continuation is confirmed when price closes below the rim.

patterns.name: Rising Wedge (continuation)
patterns.context: downtrend interrupted by a corrective rally whose support and resistance lines both rise but converge
patterns.answerLine: Wedge support breaks. Downtrend resumes.
patterns.ruleText: A rising wedge inside a downtrend is a corrective rally where both boundary lines slope upward but the range narrows, support rising faster than resistance. Continuation of the downtrend is confirmed when a candle closes below the wedge's rising support line.

patterns.name: Symmetrical Triangle
patterns.context: uptrend into a converging triangle — descending highs meeting ascending lows
patterns.answerLine: Coil resolves with the prior trend, upward.
patterns.ruleText: A symmetrical triangle is a coil of descending highs and ascending lows converging toward an apex, with no clear side favored until it breaks. Continuation of the prior uptrend is confirmed when a candle closes back above the triangle's upper boundary.

patterns.name: Measured Move
patterns.context: an impulsive leg up, a partial correction, then a base — the next leg is expected to travel a similar distance
patterns.answerLine: Leg two breaks out, measuring against leg one.
patterns.ruleText: A measured move is an impulsive leg, a corrective pullback, then a second impulsive leg that tends to travel a distance similar to the first, measured from the correction's low. Continuation is confirmed when price closes back above the first leg's high.

patterns.name: Common Gap
patterns.context: a quiet, range-bound market with no clear trend
patterns.answerLine: Small gap inside the range. Filled next bar.
patterns.ruleText: A small gap appears inside an existing trading range rather than at a breakout point. It carries no trend significance if it gets filled within a bar or two and price simply resumes drifting inside the same range instead of trending away from it.

patterns.name: Gap and Go
patterns.context: a short base just under a well-defined high, with strong momentum behind the move
patterns.answerLine: Gapped over the base, closed strong every bar.
patterns.ruleText: Price gaps up over the high of a short base and never looks back. Confirmation is each following bar closing in the upper part of its own range with no pullback into the gap, showing sustained buying pressure rather than a one-bar spike.

patterns.name: Breakaway Gap (Bearish)
patterns.context: a sideways range above support, tested three times and rejected
patterns.answerLine: Gapped clean under support. No fill, no hesitation.
patterns.ruleText: Price coils above a well-tested support level, then gaps down and opens below it with no overlap to the prior candle. The move is confirmed only if the days that follow hold below the gap and never trade back into it.

patterns.name: Breakaway Gap (Bullish)
patterns.context: a sideways range under resistance, tested three times and rejected
patterns.answerLine: Gapped clean over resistance. No fill, no hesitation.
patterns.ruleText: Price coils under a well-tested resistance level, then gaps up and opens above it with no overlap to the prior candle. The move is confirmed only if the days that follow hold above the gap and never trade back into it.

patterns.name: Falling Window
patterns.context: a steady, orderly downtrend that opens a gap and keeps declining
patterns.answerLine: Bounced to the window, got capped, rolled over.
patterns.ruleText: A downtrend opens a gap, or window, between two candles. Confirmation comes on the retest: when price later bounces toward the window, the high must stay below the window's ceiling rather than trading back through it, after which the trend resumes lower.

patterns.name: Gap Fill
patterns.context: a breakout attempt above a level that had held for many prior bars
patterns.answerLine: Broke out on a gap, then gave it back.
patterns.ruleText: Price gaps above a prior level on a breakout attempt, but instead of holding, the next bars reverse and trade back through the gap. Confirmation is a close below the pre-gap level, meaning the gap is fully filled and the breakout failed.

patterns.name: Rising Window
patterns.context: a steady, orderly uptrend that opens a gap and keeps climbing
patterns.answerLine: Pulled back to the window and held. Pushed higher.
patterns.ruleText: An uptrend opens a gap, or window, between two candles. Confirmation comes on the retest: when price later pulls back toward the window, the low must hold above the window's floor rather than trading back through it, after which the trend resumes higher.

patterns.name: Exhaustion Gap (Bearish Trend)
patterns.context: the final stretch of a long, extended downtrend that has been declining for many bars
patterns.answerLine: Last gasp lower, then given right back. Spent.
patterns.ruleText: After a long decline, price gaps down one more time but the move has no follow-through. Confirmation is the next bars reversing hard and closing above the level the gap started from, filling the gap and signaling sellers have run out.

patterns.name: Exhaustion Gap (Bullish Trend)
patterns.context: the final stretch of a long, extended uptrend that has been climbing for many bars
patterns.answerLine: Last gasp higher, then given right back. Spent.
patterns.ruleText: After a long advance, price gaps up one more time but the move has no follow-through. Confirmation is the next bars reversing hard and closing below the level the gap started from, filling the gap and signaling buyers have run out.

patterns.name: Island Reversal (Bottom)
patterns.context: the bottom of an extended downtrend, where price gaps into a brief low cluster
patterns.answerLine: Gapped in, stalled, gapped out. Island stranded.
patterns.ruleText: Price gaps down into a tight cluster of bars at the bottom, then gaps back up without the two gaps ever overlapping, leaving that cluster stranded as an island. Confirmation is the up-gap's low staying above the island's high, with price continuing higher after.

patterns.name: Island Reversal (Top)
patterns.context: the top of an extended uptrend, where price gaps into a brief high cluster
patterns.answerLine: Gapped in, stalled, gapped out. Island stranded.
patterns.ruleText: Price gaps up into a tight cluster of bars at the top, then gaps back down without the two gaps ever overlapping, leaving that cluster stranded as an island. Confirmation is the down-gap's high staying below the island's low, with price continuing lower after.

patterns.name: Three Gaps Exhaustion
patterns.context: an uptrend that has already produced two clean up-gaps and is stretching for a third
patterns.answerLine: Third gap in the trend. Usually the last one.
patterns.ruleText: A trend produces a third same-direction gap after already showing two earlier ones. Confirmation is the bar right after the third gap closing back below that gap's low, since a third consecutive gap this close together often marks the trend running out of participants.

patterns.name: Consolidation Breakout
patterns.context: price chops sideways in a well-defined range, testing the ceiling four times without breaking it, before a strong candle finally clears it
patterns.answerLine: Range broke up. Momentum candle cleared the ceiling.
patterns.ruleText: After price chops sideways between a well-tested support and resistance, a candle finally closes decisively beyond one edge of the range with real momentum, not just a wick. A close beyond the range, followed by continuation, confirms the sideways phase has resolved.

patterns.name: Failed Breakout / Fakeout
patterns.context: uptrend grinds into a resistance level, tests it twice and gets rejected both times, then pokes through it on the next attempt
patterns.answerLine: Breakout failed. Price closed back below resistance.
patterns.ruleText: Price pokes above resistance but cannot hold: the very next candle closes back below the broken level. A breakout that fails to hold within a candle or two is a fakeout, and it often reverses the false move entirely.

patterns.name: Liquidity Sweep / Stop Hunt
patterns.context: price grinds sideways-to-up above a well-defined swing low that has held twice, then wicks sharply through it before snapping back
patterns.answerLine: Stops swept below the low, then reclaimed fast.
patterns.ruleText: Price wicks sharply below a prior swing low, the level where resting stop-loss orders cluster, then closes back above that low within the same candle. The long lower wick and fast reclaim signal the move was a liquidity grab, not a real breakdown.

patterns.name: Bear Trap
patterns.context: steady downtrend chops into a tight range above a support level, breaks below it drawing in sellers, then reverses hard
patterns.answerLine: Trapped shorts. Price broke the range high next.
patterns.ruleText: Price breaks below a support level, drawing in breakdown sellers, then reverses hard and closes back above the level within a candle or two. Confirmation is a decisive close back above the prior trading range's high, trapping those who sold the breakdown.

patterns.name: Break of Structure (BOS)
patterns.context: an established uptrend of higher highs and higher lows pulls back to a fresh higher low and consolidates just under the last swing high
patterns.answerLine: Prior swing high broken. Uptrend structure confirmed.
patterns.ruleText: In an established uptrend, price pulls back to a higher low, consolidates, then closes decisively above the most recent swing high. That close above the prior high is a break of structure, confirmation the trend is continuing rather than reversing.

patterns.name: Breakout and Retest
patterns.context: steady uptrend runs into a resistance level tested three times, finally breaks out, then pulls back to retest the broken level from above
patterns.answerLine: Retest held as support. Buyers stepped back in.
patterns.ruleText: After a breakout above a resistance level, price often pulls back to retest that level from above. If the retest holds and price closes back above the level, the old resistance has flipped to support and the breakout is confirmed.

patterns.name: Bull Trap
patterns.context: strong uptrend chops into a tight range under a resistance level, breaks above it drawing in buyers, then reverses hard
patterns.answerLine: Trapped longs. Price broke the range low next.
patterns.ruleText: Price breaks above a resistance level, drawing in breakout buyers, then reverses hard and closes back below the level within a candle or two. Confirmation is a decisive close back under the prior trading range's low, trapping those who bought the breakout.

patterns.name: Change of Character (CHoCH)
patterns.context: an uptrend of higher highs and higher lows pulls back into a minor consolidation sitting just above the last confirmed higher low
patterns.answerLine: Last higher low broken. Character changed to bearish.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend of higher highs and higher lows, the first candle to close below the most recent higher low breaks that pattern. This break of the last confirmed higher low is a change of character, an early structural clue the uptrend may be reversing.

patterns.name: Higher-High Higher-Low Continuation
patterns.context: a clean uptrend printing a series of rising swing highs and rising swing lows, pulling back to the latest higher low before pressing on
patterns.answerLine: Another higher low held. Structure still points up.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend, each swing high prints above the last swing high, and each swing low prints above the last swing low. As long as this higher-high, higher-low sequence continues, the trend's structure is intact and pullbacks are being bought before new highs.

patterns.name: Lower-High Lower-Low Breakdown
patterns.context: a clean downtrend printing a series of falling swing highs and falling swing lows, bouncing to the latest lower high before rolling over again
patterns.answerLine: Another lower high held. Structure still points down.
patterns.ruleText: In a downtrend, each swing high prints below the last swing high, and each swing low prints below the last swing low. As long as this lower-high, lower-low sequence continues, the trend's structure is intact and bounces are being sold before new lows.

patterns.name: Range Expansion
patterns.context: price coils in a tight, low-volatility sideways band for many bars before one candle prints a much larger range than the recent average
patterns.answerLine: Range tripled. Compression broke into a real move.
patterns.ruleText: After a stretch of small, tight-range candles showing low volatility and indecision, one candle prints a much larger range than the recent average and closes near its extreme. That expansion signals compression has resolved, often starting a new directional move.

patterns.name: Trendline Break and Retest
patterns.context: a downtrend follows a clean descending trendline touched by three lower swing highs, then a candle closes decisively above the line and price pulls back to test it
patterns.answerLine: Trendline broken, retested as support, then held.
patterns.ruleText: A descending trendline connecting a series of lower highs is broken by a strong close above it. Price then pulls back to touch the same trendline from above; if it holds as new support and price closes higher, the downtrend's structure has broken.

patterns.name: Spring (Wyckoff)
patterns.context: price chops inside a well-tested trading range, dipping to test the range's support floor three times before one candle wicks decisively through it
patterns.answerLine: Support undercut, then reclaimed. Weak hands shaken out.
patterns.ruleText: Inside a Wyckoff trading range, price briefly wicks below the range's support floor, undercutting prior tests, then closes back inside the range above support. This spring shakes out late sellers before the range resolves higher, a hallmark of accumulation.

patterns.name: Upthrust (Wyckoff)
patterns.context: price chops inside a well-tested trading range, poking up to test the range's resistance ceiling three times before one candle wicks decisively above it
patterns.answerLine: Resistance overshot, then rejected. Late buyers trapped.
patterns.ruleText: Inside a Wyckoff trading range, price briefly wicks above the range's resistance ceiling, overshooting prior tests, then closes back inside the range below resistance. This upthrust traps late buyers before the range resolves lower, a hallmark of distribution.

patterns.name: Moving Average Bounce
patterns.context: a steady uptrend pulls back to touch its rising moving average and holds
patterns.answerLine: Price tagged the rising average and held.
patterns.ruleText: In a steady uptrend, a pullback candle dips down to touch the rising moving average and closes back above it. Confirmation is the next candles resuming the prior trend's direction rather than closing through the average.

patterns.name: Overbought Rejection at Resistance
patterns.context: an uptrend tests the same resistance level twice, with the RSI reading overbought on the second test
patterns.answerLine: Second test of resistance, RSI overbought, sellers stepped in.
patterns.ruleText: Price returns to a resistance level already tested once before, this time with the RSI reading above 70. A rejection candle that fails at the level and closes back below it, followed by a lower close, confirms sellers stepped back in.

patterns.name: Oversold Bounce at Support
patterns.context: a downtrend tests the same support level twice, with the RSI reading oversold on the second test
patterns.answerLine: Second test of support, RSI oversold, price held.
patterns.ruleText: Price returns to a support level already tested once before, this time with the RSI reading below 30. A bounce candle that holds the level and closes back above it, followed by a higher close, confirms buyers stepped back in.

patterns.name: Volume Dry-Up Breakout
patterns.context: an uptrend pauses into a tight, narrowing consolidation before a decisive breakout candle
patterns.answerLine: Range tightened for days, then broke out up.
patterns.ruleText: Trading range compresses into a series of small, overlapping candles as volatility contracts. A wide-range candle that closes above the range high, on the first burst of participation after the dry-up, signals the range is resolving higher.

patterns.name: Bollinger Band Walk
patterns.context: a strong uptrend pushes closes to ride along the upper Bollinger Band for several bars in a row
patterns.answerLine: Closes kept riding the upper band, bar after bar.
patterns.ruleText: In a strong trend, consecutive closes sit at or beyond the upper Bollinger Band instead of reverting to the middle band. This band walk signals persistent momentum; it is not, by itself, an overbought sell signal.

patterns.name: Bollinger Squeeze Breakout
patterns.context: Bollinger Bands compress to their narrowest width of the sequence as price coils in a tight range
patterns.answerLine: Bands squeezed tight, then price broke out up.
patterns.ruleText: Bollinger Band width contracts to its tightest reading of the sequence as price coils in a narrow range. Confirmation is a wide-range candle closing outside the upper band as the bands begin expanding again, not merely touching the band.

patterns.name: Death Cross
patterns.context: an uptrend tops into a base and the faster moving average rolls over through the slower one
patterns.answerLine: Fast moving average crossed below the slow one.
patterns.ruleText: After an uptrend tops out, the shorter-term moving average rolls over and crosses below the longer-term moving average. The cross is confirmed on the candle where the fast average closes below the slow one, not on the approach toward it.

patterns.name: Golden Cross
patterns.context: a downtrend bottoms into a base and the faster moving average curls back up through the slower one
patterns.answerLine: Fast moving average crossed above the slow one.
patterns.ruleText: After a downtrend bases out, the shorter-term moving average turns up and crosses above the longer-term moving average. The cross is confirmed on the candle where the fast average closes above the slow one, not on the approach toward it.

patterns.name: MACD Bullish Crossover
patterns.context: a downtrend flattens into a base and the MACD line turns up through its signal line
patterns.answerLine: MACD line crossed above its signal line.
patterns.ruleText: The MACD line (the difference between two moving averages) crosses above its signal line after a downtrend flattens out. Confirmation is the crossover holding for more than one bar, together with price closing back above the base it built.

patterns.name: Bearish RSI Divergence
patterns.context: an uptrend prints a new price high while the RSI fails to make a new high
patterns.answerLine: New price high, but momentum peaked lower.
patterns.ruleText: Price prints a higher high than the prior swing, but the RSI prints a lower high at the same point. That gap between price and momentum is the divergence; it is confirmed only once price turns down and breaks the recent swing low.

patterns.name: Bullish RSI Divergence
patterns.context: a downtrend prints a new price low while the RSI fails to make a new low
patterns.answerLine: Price fell further, but momentum did not follow.
patterns.ruleText: Price prints a lower low than the prior swing, but the RSI prints a higher low at the same point. That gap between price and momentum is the divergence; it is confirmed only once price turns up and breaks the recent swing high.

patterns.name: Hidden Bullish Divergence
patterns.context: an established uptrend pulls back to a higher price low while the RSI dips to a deeper low
patterns.answerLine: Higher low in price, deeper low in momentum.
patterns.ruleText: In an uptrend, a pullback holds above the prior swing low (a higher low in price) even though the RSI dips below its prior reading (a lower low in momentum). This hidden divergence favors trend continuation once price resumes making new highs.
